state.work_item: Re-roof the main pitched roof with new tiles and membrane
state.jurisdiction: England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.

clauses.text: 16. Installation, as a replacement, of the covering of a pitched or flat roof and work carried out by the registered person as a necessary adjunct to that installation. This paragraph does not apply to the installation of solar panels. | A person registered in respect of that type of work by NAPIT Registration Limited or the National Federation of Roofing Contractors Limited.

11.2 Renovation of a thermal element means one of the following. a. Providing a new layer through cladding or rendering the external surface of a thermal element. b. Providing a new layer through dry-lining the internal surface of a thermal element. c. Replacing an existing layer through stripping down the element to expose basic structural components (e.g. bricks, blocks, rafters, joists, frame) and then rebuilding. d. Replacing the waterproof membrane on a flat roof. e. Providing cavity wall insulation.

0.16 Provide loft insulation – 250mm mineral fibre or cellulose fibre as a quilt laid between and across ceiling joists or loose fill or equivalent. This may be boarded out Assess condensation risk in roof space and make appropriate provision in accordance with the requirements of Part C relating to the control of condensation (BS 5250 and BS EN ISO 13788). Additional provision may be required to provide insulation and access to services in the roof void Cold structure – insulation (thickness dependent on material) placed between and below rafters Assess condensation risk (particularly interstitial condensation) and make appropriate provision in accordance with the requirements of Part C relating to the control of condensation (BS 5250 and BS EN ISO 13788) Warm structure – insulation placed between and above rafters Where there is an increase in structural thickness (particularly in terraced dwellings), practical considerations may necessitate a lower performance target Renewal of roof covering: Living accommodation in roof space (room-in-the-roof arrangement), with or without dormer windows

route.instructions: Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

criteria.not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
criteria.competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
criteria.building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
criteria.full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
